marcus: quick heads-up — ran a cpu-side profile against the host ingress for the noisy p99s. host tokenization + request parse + framing = ~24% of tail p99 on our mid-size traffic shape. stack: http2 -> ingress parser -> tokenize -> kv cache lookup -> enqueue to runtime
anya: ouch. do you see if any single function dominates?
sasha: earlier traces showed heavy memcpy / string split during tokenization, plus a few syscalls around readv/writev when streaming chunks. also a pathological case where small fragments triggered full JSON parse path.
marcus: exact flame had big hotspots at tokenize_frame(), parse_request_headers(), and grpc_frame_writer::flush(). attached small snippet: ```text
tokenize_frame  46ms
parse_request_headers  28ms
kv_lookup_prefetch  12ms
grpc_frame_writer::flush  38ms
```
anya: can we avoid full JSON parse for streaming chunks? maybe a fast-path that treats single-chunk requests as pre-validated?
sasha: we already have a slim parser flag but it wasn't enabled for our ingress path because of legacy auth checks. toggling it reduced parse time by ~40% in local replay.
perf-bot: replay-job #11845: throughput +6% latency p95 -4% when slim-parser is enabled (no auth flow).
marcus: idea: combine two things — (1) enable slim-path for chunked streaming with auth preconditions, (2) hint kernel selection to prefer a lower-latency matmul kernel for short sequences so we avoid batching that increases latency. both should reduce host pressure and kernel-level tail.
anya: kernel hinting is tricky — need to preserve batching heuristics for throughput customers. maybe make hint opt-in by config per route?
sasha: agreed. also noticed kv-cache prefetching cost spikes when tokenization emits many small keys. we should aggregate key lookups and do a batch-kv API call to avoid syscall churn.
marcus: next steps: 1) small PR to enable slim-parser behind a feature-flag + gating test (anya), 2) prototype route-level kernel-hint config (sasha), 3) change kv client to support batch-prefetch (marcus). I'll add tickets.
ci-bot: created tickets INF-412, INF-413, INF-414 and linked this thread.
anya: I'll own INF-412 and add perf regression tests. tagging @sasha for INF-413. thanks all :thumbsup:
